paras.en: Just as leaves that fall from different trees have distinct shapes and hues of crimson or gold, tree species vary in how susceptible they are to weather. Sugar maples, a “superstar” of New England leaf peeping, are extremely sensitive to temperature and precipitation, Finton says. Oak trees, on the other hand, are more tolerant. But there’s a lot that scientists still don’t understand about how different trees are affected.
paras.zh: 正如不同树木落下的叶子具有不同的形状和深红色或金色的色调一样，树种对天气的敏感程度也有所不同。芬顿说，糖枫是新英格兰观叶的“超级明星”，对温度和降水极其敏感。另一方面，橡树则更加宽容。但科学家们仍然不明白不同的树木是如何受到影响的。

paras.en: A question Rollinson is curious about is how much of the changing of trees’ leaves is related to temperature versus sunlight—and what fall foliage might reveal about the overall health of a given tree and its ecosystem.
paras.zh: 罗林森好奇的一个问题是，树木叶子的变化在多大程度上与温度和阳光有关，以及秋天的树叶可能揭示特定树木及其生态系统的整体健康状况。

paras.en: The effect of wildfires on foliage are also little understood, says William Keeton, a forest ecologist at the University of Vermont. Early research suggests that smoke from these disasters can blow onto trees across the country and coat leaves, blocking sunlight and interfering with photosynthesis.
paras.zh: 佛蒙特大学森林生态学家威廉·基顿表示，人们对野火对树叶的影响也知之甚少。早期研究表明，这些灾难产生的烟雾可能会吹到全国各地的树木上并覆盖叶子，阻挡阳光并干扰光合作用。

paras.en: This year the Midwest has seen a vast variety of weather conditions, from extreme heat to massive tornadoes to heavy rainfall, so it’s difficult to know how the trees there will react, Rollinson says.
paras.zh: 罗林森说，今年中西部出现了各种各样的天气状况，从极端高温到大规模龙卷风再到强降雨，因此很难知道那里的树木会如何反应。

paras.en: “Normally I’m able to make some general statements about the health of trees going into the fall, but I think there’s a huge variation because each tree will respond to those stressors a little bit differently,” she says.
paras.zh: “通常情况下，我能够对树木进入秋季的健康状况做出一些一般性的陈述，但我认为存在巨大的差异，因为每棵树对这些压力的反应都略有不同，”她说。

paras.en: In New England, meanwhile, the summer saw extreme heat and some drought. But because, so far, this fall has been “cooler, crisper and clearer,” Finton says, the leaves are coming in right on time, and he expects a relatively typical foliage season.
paras.zh: 与此同时，在新英格兰，夏季出现了极端炎热和干旱。但芬顿说，因为到目前为止，今年的秋天“更凉爽、更清脆、更清澈”，树叶准时长出来，他预计将是一个相对典型的树叶季节。

paras.en: Most of the northern U.S. is seeing peak foliage colors this week. The mid-Atlantic and Midwest regions can expect the best leaf peeping in the second half of October.
paras.zh: 本周，美国北部大部分地区的树叶颜色将达到高峰。大西洋中部和中西部地区预计十月下旬是最佳赏叶季节。

articles.title: Voyager 1 is nearly one light-day from Earth. What’s out there?
articles.author: Lisa Grossman

paras.en: NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft has been breaking distance records for decades. Launched almost 50 years ago, it became the farthest human-built object from Earth when it overtook the pathfinding Pioneer 10 probe in 1998. It was the first spacecraft to leave the solar system’s protective bubble, and it will be humankind’s first emissary to the stars.
paras.zh: 美国国家航空航天局 (NASA) 的航行者 1 号航天器几十年来一直在打破距离记录。它发射近 50 年前，于 1998 年超越了探路先锋 10 号探测器，成为距地球最远的人造物体。它是第一艘离开太阳系保护层的航天器，也将成为人类第一位前往星际的使者。

paras.en: The cameras on Voyager 1, along with those on its twin spacecraft, Voyager 2, captured powerful megastorms in the outer solar system, the first images of dozens of moons and never-before-seen details of the gossamer rings around Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune and Uranus. The images and data sent home have shaped theories of how the solar system formed and evolved, inspired subsequent missions and posed enough new questions to keep space scientists busy for decades.
paras.zh: 航海者一号及其孪生航天器航海者二号上的相机捕捉到了太阳系外层强大的超级风暴、数十颗卫星的第一张图像以及木星、土星、海王星和天王星周围薄纱环的前所未见的细节。发送回国的图像和数据塑造了太阳系如何形成和演化的理论，启发了后续的任务，并提出了足够多的新问题，让太空科学家忙了几十年。

paras.en: And this month, Voyager 1 will set another big record. On November 18 at 5:16:07 a.m. Eastern Standard Time, it will become the first spacecraft to reach one light-day from Earth: the distance light travels in 24 hours. That’s a journey of 25.9 billion kilometers, or more than four times the distance from the sun to Pluto. At that point, signals from Earth will take a full day to reach Voyager 1; it will take another day to hear back.
paras.zh: 本月，航海家一号将创下另一项重大纪录。东部标准时间 11 月 18 日凌晨 5:16:07，它将成为第一个距离地球达到一光日的航天器：光在 24 小时内传播的距离。这是 259 亿公里的旅程，是太阳到冥王星距离的四倍多。届时，来自地球的信号将需要一整天才能到达旅行者一号；又要一天才能收到回复。

paras.en: “I just never imagined [the mission] would last that long,” says Linda Spilker, a planetary scientist at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Pasadena, Calif., who began working on Voyager shortly before the probes launched in 1977. Spilker was in Cape Canaveral, Fla., for the first launch. She even planned the births of her children, now in their 40s, around mission milestones. After stepping away to lead another mission, she is now back as Voyager head scientist.
paras.zh: “我只是没想到（这次任务）会持续那么久，”美国宇航局加利福尼亚州帕萨迪纳喷气推进实验室的行星科学家琳达·斯皮尔克（Linda Spilker）说道，她在 1977 年探测器发射前不久就开始从事航行者号的工作。斯皮尔克在佛罗里达州卡纳维拉尔角进行了首次发射。她甚至围绕任务里程碑计划了自己 40 多岁孩子的出生。在离开领导另一项任务后，她现在重新担任航行者号首席科学家。

paras.en: Two other scientists have been with Voyager since the beginning. Others weren’t yet born when the spacecraft launched. “Voyager, to this day, is a multi-generational mission,” Spilker says. But it isn’t a mission of nostalgia. There’s still a world of discovery out beyond the solar system’s edge.
paras.zh: 另外两名科学家从一开始就一直在航海者号工作。当宇宙飞船发射时，其他人还没有出生。 “时至今日，Voyager 仍是一项需要几代人共同努力的任务，”Spilker 说道。但这不是怀旧的使命。太阳系边缘之外仍然有一个值得探索的世界。

paras.en: “Every piece of data, every day that goes by that we get data from the Voyagers, tells us something new,” says physicist Jamie Rankin of Princeton University, who started her Ph.D. in August 2012, the same month that Voyager 1 left the solar system for the cold, calm seas of interstellar space. “Every day, it’s in places nobody’s ever explored before.”
paras.zh: 普林斯顿大学的物理学家杰米·兰金 (Jamie Rankin) 说：“我们从航行者号获得的数据的每一天、每一天，都告诉我们一些新的东西。” 2012 年 8 月，航行者一号离开太阳系，前往寒冷、平静的星际空间海洋。 “每天，它都会出现在以前没有人探索过的地方。”

paras.en: The original mission of the Voyager probes was to explore the outer parts of our solar system, which until then had remained largely mysterious. A rare planetary alignment meant that a spacecraft launched in the late 1970s could swoop past Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, getting a gravitational boost from each planet that it passed. With these gravitational assists, the spacecraft could complete the tour in less than 15 years. Such an alignment won’t happen again until the 2150s.
paras.zh: 航行者号探测器的最初任务是探索太阳系的外部部分，在此之前，该部分在很大程度上仍然是神秘的。罕见的行星排列意味着 20 世纪 70 年代末发射的航天器可以飞越木星、土星、天王星和海王星，并从其经过的每颗行星获得引力助推。有了这些引力的帮助，飞船可以在不到 15 年的时间内完成这次旅行。这种排列直到 2150 年代才会再次发生。

paras.en: The project was a bold step for its time. When work began in the early 1970s, no spacecraft had gone farther than Mars. NASA set a conservative goal for the mission: flybys of Jupiter and Saturn. In 1972 and 1973, NASA launched two Pioneer probes, which made sure the trek was possible and gathered data along the way. As with Voyager, there were two spacecraft in case one failed.
paras.zh: 该项目在当时是一个大胆的一步。当工作于 20 世纪 70 年代初开始时，还没有航天器飞得比火星更远。美国宇航局为该任务设定了一个保守的目标：飞越木星和土星。 1972 年和 1973 年，美国宇航局发射了两个先锋探测器，确保了这次长途跋涉的可能性，并沿途收集了数据。与航行者号一样，有两艘航天器以防其中一艘失败。

paras.en: After nail-biting launches and a wait of nearly two years, the Voyagers began uncovering many of Jupiter’s and Saturn’s long-held secrets, including the volcanoes on Jupiter’s moon Io, details of Jupiter’s Great Red Spot and hints of geologic activity on Saturn’s moon Enceladus.
paras.zh: 经过紧张的发射和近两年的等待，航海者号开始揭开木星和土星的许多长期秘密，包括木星卫星木卫一上的火山、木星大红斑的细节以及土星卫星土卫二上地质活动的迹象。

paras.en: Mission accomplished, Voyager 2 went on to pass Uranus and Neptune. It took the first images of the planets’ rings and discovered more than a dozen moons along the way. The spacecraft also spotted a perpetually churning storm on Neptune and erupting geysers on Neptune’s moon Triton.
paras.zh: 任务完成后，航海家二号继续飞越天王星和海王星。它拍摄了第一张行星环的图像，并沿途发现了十多个卫星。该航天器还发现海王星上有一场持续翻腾的风暴，并在海王星的卫星海卫一上发现了间歇泉。

paras.en: “The highlights of Voyager were clearly the planetary encounters,” said Ed Stone, the mission’s original head scientist, in a NASA interview before his death in 2024. “We had a lifetime of discovery packed into each one.”
paras.zh: “航行者号的亮点显然是行星相遇，”该任务最初的首席科学家埃德·斯通 (Ed Stone) 在 2024 年去世前接受 NASA 采访时说道，“每一次探索都蕴含着我们一生的发现。”

paras.en: The uncontested stars of these encounters were the images shared in news reports and TV broadcasts as the planets and their moons came into view. Jupiter’s moon Io turned out to be a shocking splotchy orange color that looked like a pizza.
paras.zh: 这些相遇中无可争议的明星是当行星及其卫星进入视野时在新闻报道和电视广播中分享的图像。木星的卫星木卫一呈令人震惊的斑点橙色，看起来像披萨。

paras.en: A humble navigation image of that moon led to one of the most surprising discoveries of the entire mission. Four days past Voyager 1’s closest approach to Jupiter, after the excitement had died down, project astronomer Linda Morabito of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory started processing additional images of Io. These images had been taken after the flyby, when Voyager was looking back over its shoulder.
paras.zh: 那颗卫星的一张简陋的导航图像带来了整个任务中最令人惊讶的发现之一。航海者一号最接近木星四天后，兴奋消退后，喷气推进实验室的项目天文学家琳达·莫拉比托开始处理木卫一的更多图像。这些照片是在飞越之后拍摄的，当时航行者号回头望去。

paras.en: As Morabito enhanced one image’s brightness, she spotted an odd bulbous formation protruding from Io’s edge. “What’s that?” she asked herself. Her supervisor had the same reaction: “Jesus, what’s that?” she later recalled him saying.
paras.zh: 当莫拉比托增强了一张图像的亮度时，她发现了一个奇怪的球状结构从木卫一的边缘突出。 “那是什么？”她问自己。她的主管也有同样的反应：“天哪，那是什么？”她后来回忆起他说的话。

paras.en: The bulb turned out to be a volcanic plume — an erupting fire fountain extending 250 kilometers above Io’s surface. It was the first discovery of active volcanism anywhere other than Earth, and it transformed our view of the outer solar system. Instead of a cold, inert icebox, this was a bubbling and dynamic region.
paras.zh: 事实证明，这个灯泡是火山羽流——一个喷发的火焰喷泉，延伸到木卫一表面上方 250 公里处。这是在地球以外的任何地方首次发现活火山活动，它改变了我们对外太阳系的看法。这里不是一个冰冷、惰性的冰箱，而是一个冒泡、充满活力的区域。

paras.en: The findings inspired many future missions. While visiting Jupiter from 1995 to 2003, the Galileo probe found that Europa may have a subsurface ocean that could be hospitable to life. When the Cassini probe orbited Saturn from 2004 to 2017, it discovered that the moon Enceladus also has a potentially habitable ocean that spews icy geysers into space.
paras.zh: 这些发现启发了许多未来的任务。伽利略号探测器在 1995 年至 2003 年访问木星时发现木卫二可能存在适合生命生存的地下海洋。当卡西尼号探测器于 2004 年至 2017 年绕土星运行时，它发现土卫二卫星也有一个潜在的宜居海洋，该海洋向太空喷出冰冷的间歇泉。

paras.en: In 1990, with Voyager 1 about 6 billion kilometers from the sun, astronomer Carl Sagan convinced mission leaders to turn the spacecraft backward for one last look at the planets. Voyager 1 took a family portrait in which Earth appeared faintly as a “pale blue dot,” Sagan said. “Everyone you love, everyone you know, everyone you ever heard of, every human being who ever was, lived out their lives … on a mote of dust suspended in a sunbeam,” he wrote in the 1994 book Pale Blue Dot.
paras.zh: 1990 年，航海家一号距离太阳约 60 亿公里，天文学家卡尔·萨根说服任务领导人将航天器向后转动，以便最后一次观察行星。萨根说，航海者一号拍摄了一张全家福，其中地球隐隐约约地呈现为“淡蓝色的点”。 “你所爱的每一个人、你认识的每一个人、你听说过的每一个人、曾经存在过的每一个人，都在悬浮在阳光中的一粒尘埃上度过了自己的一生，”他在 1994 年出版的《淡蓝点》一书中写道。

paras.en: To save power, Voyager 2’s cameras were shut off in 1989. After the family portrait, Voyager 1’s cameras were also turned off. Where the spacecraft were headed, there wouldn’t be much to see.
paras.zh: 为了节省电力，航海家二号的相机在1989年被关闭。全家福之后，航海家一号的相机也被关闭。宇宙飞船所前往的地方，不会有太多可看的东西。

paras.en: The probes were now on their way out of the solar system along their own separate paths, both headed toward a mysterious boundary that no human emissary had ever crossed. In this next phase of their voyage, no one knew what to expect. How long would the spacecraft keep communicating? How far would the powerful forces that drive the sun reach? And what would it be like to taste interstellar space?
paras.zh: 探测器现在正沿着各自不同的路径离开太阳系，都朝着人类使者从未跨越过的神秘边界前进。在他们航行的下一阶段，没有人知道会发生什么。宇宙飞船还能保持通信多久？驱动太阳的强大力量能到达多远？品尝星际空间会是什么样的感觉？

paras.en: For its first 35 years in space, Voyager 1 was swaddled in the solar wind. This stream of hot, charged particles flows constantly from the sun, forming a vast bubble called the heliosphere. The bubble surrounds the solar system, protecting it from cosmic radiation; it extends billions of kilometers past the planets up to a boundary called the heliopause. Heliophysicists consider this boundary, where the solar wind bumps into interstellar space, the edge of the solar system, although the sun’s gravitational influence extends much farther.
paras.zh: 在太空航行的头 35 年里，航海者 1 号一直沐浴在太阳风中。这种炽热的带电粒子流不断从太阳中流出，形成一个巨大的气泡，称为日光层。气泡包围着太阳系，保护其免受宇宙辐射；它延伸了数十亿公里，穿过行星，到达称为日球层顶的边界。太阳物理学家认为这个边界是太阳风撞击星际空间的地方，即太阳系的边缘，尽管太阳的引力影响范围更远。

paras.en: Scientists expected the Voyagers to cross the heliopause, but they didn’t know when — or what the spacecraft would find when they did. Rankin had just started her Ph.D. at Caltech when in August 2012 Voyager 1 detected an abrupt jump in the number of high-energy cosmic rays alongside a drop in solar particles, hinting that the spacecraft had crossed the boundary. But magnetic field measurements suggested otherwise. Instead, those measurements indicated that the sun still exerted some influence. The interstellar magnetic field diverted around the heliosphere like a river around a rock.
paras.zh: 科学家们预计航海者号将穿越日球层顶，但他们不知道何时——也不知道当他们穿越时飞船会发现什么。兰金刚刚开始攻读博士学位。 2012 年 8 月，航行者 1 号在加州理工学院检测到高能宇宙射线数量突然增加，同时太阳粒子数量下降，这暗示航天器已经跨越了边界。但磁场测量表明情况并非如此。相反，这些测量表明太阳仍然施加了一些影响。星际磁场在日光层周围转移，就像河流围绕岩石一样。

paras.en: A Voyager instrument that could have settled the question of whether the probe had passed the heliopause was no longer working. But scientists got a lucky break in April 2013 when an eruption on the sun sent a pressure wave rippling outward. It set the electrons around Voyager 1 vibrating, which allowed scientists to estimate the density of charged particles nearby.
paras.zh: 原本可以解决探测器是否已通过日球层顶问题的航行者号仪器已不再工作。但科学家们在 2013 年 4 月迎来了一次幸运的突破，当时太阳的喷发发出了向外扩散的压力波。它使航行者一号周围的电子振动，从而使科学家能够估计附近带电粒子的密度。

paras.en: The results showed that Voyager 1 had in fact crossed the heliopause on August 25, 2012, when it was about 18 billion kilometers away, or 120 times Earth’s distance from the sun. Data from Voyager 2 later backed up that finding. “This is the beginning of a new era of exploration for us,” Stone told Science News in 2013.
paras.zh: 结果显示，航海家一号实际上已于 2012 年 8 月 25 日穿越日球层顶，当时距离太阳约 180 亿公里，是地球与太阳距离的 120 倍。来自航行者 2 号的数据后来支持了这一发现。 “这对我们来说是探索新时代的开始，”斯通在 2013 年告诉《科学新闻》。

paras.en: But the line between our solar system and interstellar space isn’t solid. The sun’s reach extends farther than anyone expected, and “this boundary is not very sharp or very thin,” says physicist Jeewoo Park of NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Md.
paras.zh: 但我们的太阳系和星际空间之间的界限并不牢固。马里兰州格林贝尔特美国宇航局戈达德太空飞行中心的物理学家 Jeewoo Park 表示，太阳的覆盖范围比任何人预期的都要远，而且“这个边界并不是很尖锐或很薄”。

paras.en: With Voyager on the other side of the heliopause, particle speeds and gas temperatures have dropped. The magnetic field is weaker. Even dust particles are about half as abundant compared with inside the heliosphere. “For the most part, it’s been very quiet and very consistent,” Rankin says.
paras.zh: 随着航海者号位于日球层顶的另一侧，粒子速度和气体温度都下降了。磁场较弱。即使是尘埃颗粒的数量也只有日光层内部的一半左右。 “在大多数情况下，它非常安静且非常一致，”兰金说。

paras.en: But it’s not entirely silent. In four instances, scientists saw spikes in the magnetic field strength and particle density measurements around the probe. After the fourth, in mid-2020, those numbers have remained high. No one knows why. Perhaps Voyager 1 continues to ride the aftershocks of solar eruptions, says Park, who reported on the events in June in the Astrophysical Journal.
paras.zh: 但它并非完全沉默。在四个例子中，科学家们发现探测器周围的磁场强度和粒子密度测量值出现峰值。在 2020 年中期第四次之后，这些数字仍然很高。没有人知道为什么。帕克说，也许旅行者一号会继续承受太阳喷发的余震，他在六月份的《天体物理学杂志》上报道了这一事件。

paras.en: Where pure interstellar space begins is still an open question. So is the heliosphere’s shape. Most scientists think it is elongated, like a comet, but others think it is a sphere or even a croissant.
paras.zh: 纯粹的星际空间从哪里开始仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。日光层的形状也是如此。大多数科学家认为它是细长的，就像彗星一样，但也有人认为它是一个球体，甚至是一个羊角面包。

paras.en: Space telescopes launched in 2008 and 2025, the Interstellar Boundary Explorer and Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe, could help answer that question.
paras.zh: 2008 年和 2025 年发射的太空望远镜、星际边界探测器和星际测绘与加速探测器可以帮助回答这个问题。

paras.en: Meanwhile, the Voyager probes are silently sailing onward. Scientists estimate that the onboard power sources that keep the crafts’ instruments running will dry up in 10 to 15 years, preventing them from sending data back to Earth. Our conversation will come to an end. But the journey goes on.
paras.zh: 与此同时，航海者号探测器正在悄然前行。科学家估计，维持飞船仪器运行的机载电源将在 10 到 15 年内枯竭，导致它们无法将数据发送回地球。我们的谈话将结束。但旅程仍在继续。

paras.en: Voyager 2 will approach a red dwarf star known as Ross 248 in about 42,000 years, coming within 700 light-days. It will be 44,000 years before Voyager 1 next encounters another star, Gliese 445, at a similar distance. “The Voyagers become our silent ambassadors, a little bit of us that continues into space,” Spilker says.
paras.zh: 航海者 2 号将在大约 42,000 年后接近一颗名为 Ross 248 的红矮星，距离不到 700 光日。 44,000 年后，航海家 1 号在相似的距离下再次遇到另一颗恒星 Gliese 445。 “航行者号成为我们沉默的大使，是我们继续进入太空的一部分，”斯皮尔克说。

paras.en: They carry a message, should anyone find it, contained on the Golden Record. A copy of the phonograph record, which is plated in gold, rides on each of the probes. The long-distance dispatches feature sights and sounds of Earth, including a map of the solar system; images of Earth’s monuments; greetings in dozens of languages; and the sounds of whale song, laughter, classical composers and Navajo chants.
paras.zh: 它们携带着金唱片中包含的信息，如果有人发现的话。每个探头上都装有一张镀金的留声机唱片。远程调度以地球的景象和声音为特色，包括太阳系地图；地球古迹的图像；用数十种语言问候；还有鲸鱼的歌声、笑声、古典作曲家和纳瓦霍圣歌的声音。

paras.en: That time capsule captures the optimism and promise of the mission, Spilker says. “It may well outlast humanity.”
paras.zh: 斯皮尔克说，这个时间胶囊捕捉到了任务的乐观情绪和承诺。 “它很可能比人类更长寿。”

articles.title: Tiny implants can use the body itself to talk to each other
articles.author: Brendan Pierson

paras.en: Medical implants are getting smaller and smarter. But getting them to talk to each other remains tricky.
paras.zh: 医疗植入物变得越来越小、越来越智能。但让他们互相交谈仍然很棘手。

paras.en: Now, researchers have developed a way for tiny implantable devices to send electrical signals through the body’s own tissues. The approach could offer a low-power way for implants to work together, with one detecting a symptom and another delivering treatment, the team reports September 24 in Science.
paras.zh: 现在，研究人员已经开发出一种微型植入设备通过人体自身组织发送电信号的方法。该团队于 9 月 24 日在《科学》杂志上报道，这种方法可以为植入物提供一种低功耗的协同工作方式，其中一个植入物检测症状，另一个提供治疗。

paras.en: Currently, getting devices to communicate through tissue comes with trade-offs. Some medical devices, such as insulin pumps linked to glucose monitors, use Bluetooth, which relies on radio signals. Receiving those signals requires power even when a device is only listening, increasing the need for battery power and making devices harder shrink. Radio signals also weaken as they travel through body tissue, limiting how far apart communicating devices can be.
paras.zh: 目前，让设备通过组织进行通信需要权衡。一些医疗设备，例如与血糖监测仪连接的胰岛素泵，使用依赖于无线电信号的蓝牙。即使设备只是在监听，接收这些信号也需要电力，这增加了对电池电力的需求，并使设备更难缩小。无线电信号在穿过身体组织时也会减弱，从而限制了通信设备之间的距离。

paras.en: The new network called SWANS, the Smart Wireless Autonomous Networking System, works differently. A wearable external hub or implant generates an electric pulse that produces a small current in the surrounding tissue. Tiny implants can detect those electrical signals while using almost no power when they are only listening. And without large batteries, those implants can be small enough to inject through a syringe.
paras.zh: 名为 SWANS（智能无线自治网络系统）的新网络的工作方式有所不同。可穿戴外部集线器或植入物产生电脉冲，在周围组织中产生小电流。微小的植入物可以检测这些电信号，而当它们仅在聆听时几乎不消耗电力。如果没有大电池，这些植入物可以足够小，可以通过注射器注射。

paras.en: To demonstrate how the network works, the team attached motion sensors to the front legs of rats. When the animals moved their front legs, the system’s external hub sent signals through their bodies to neurostimulator implants in the sciatic nerves, causing muscles in the back legs to contract.
paras.zh: 为了演示该网络的工作原理，该团队将运动传感器安装在老鼠的前腿上。当动物移动前腿时，系统的外部中枢通过它们的身体向坐骨神经中的神经刺激器植入物发送信号，导致后腿的肌肉收缩。

paras.en: The synchronized limbs weren’t really the point. The experiment was designed to show that signals could travel through the body, linking different kinds of devices, says Alex Abramson, a biomedical engineer at Georgia Tech in Atlanta. It was “a proof of concept showing that you can really connect this system to anything.”
paras.zh: 同步肢体并不是真正的重点。亚特兰大佐治亚理工学院的生物医学工程师亚历克斯·艾布拉姆森 (Alex Abramson) 表示，该实验旨在证明信号可以穿过身体传播，连接不同类型的设备。这是“一个概念证明，表明你真的可以将这个系统连接到任何东西。”

paras.en: Abramson says a network of smart implants could automatically deliver a drug or stimulate a neuron exactly when needed to treat complex conditions like Parkinson’s disease. Simple signals can be sent from one implant to another, while an external hub can coordinate more complex networks of sensors and devices, possibly using artificial intelligence.
paras.zh: 艾布拉姆森说，智能植入物网络可以在需要治疗帕金森病等复杂疾病时自动输送药物或刺激神经元。简单的信号可以从一个植入物发送到另一个植入物，而外部集线器可以协调更复杂的传感器和设备网络，可能使用人工智能。

paras.en: Before the new network can be used in humans, researchers will need to show that the electrical signals do not cause unintended problems like heart rhythm disruptions. Such issues have not turned up in the experiments in rats yet, but the technology will need to be tested over longer periods of time and in larger animals, Abramson says.
paras.zh: 在新网络用于人类之前，研究人员需要证明电信号不会导致心律紊乱等意外问题。艾布拉姆森说，此类问题尚未在大鼠实验中出现，但该技术需要在更长时间和更大的动物中进行测试。

paras.en: Materials engineer Amir Alavi says the network’s potential could grow as other technologies improve, including wearables, AI systems and miniature, battery-free implantable sensors like those his lab is developing. “There are now several really interesting directions converging,” says Alavi, of at the University of Pittsburgh’s Swanson School of Engineering. “If those pieces eventually come together, you could have implants that are much smaller, simpler, longer-lived, and more connected than what we have today.”
paras.zh: 材料工程师阿米尔·阿拉维 (Amir Alavi) 表示，随着其他技术的进步，包括可穿戴设备、人工智能系统和微型无电池植入式传感器（如他的实验室正在开发的传感器），该网络的潜力可能会增长。 “现在有几个非常有趣的方向正在融合，”匹兹堡大学斯旺森工程学院的阿拉维说。 “如果这些部件最终组合在一起，你可能会拥有比我们今天的植入物更小、更简单、寿命更长、连接性更强的植入物。”

articles.title: Can math stay human in the age of AI?
articles.author: Kathryn Hulick

paras.en: “Exponentially exploding,” mathematician Thomas Bloom told me by phone, describing the flood of new results in his field. Little did he know that hours later, OpenAI was going to post 722 mathematical manuscripts an unreleased AI model had produced.
paras.zh: “呈指数级爆炸式增长，”数学家托马斯·布鲁姆在电话中告诉我，他描述了他的领域中大量的新成果。他几乎不知道几个小时后，OpenAI 将发布 722 份由未发布的 AI 模型生成的数学手稿。

paras.en: The firehose of new work lends new urgency to the question: How is AI changing mathematical discovery? In their race for headline-grabbing breakthroughs, AI companies typically do not disclose their methods and data. That competition among AI companies threatens to overwhelm human collaboration and understanding.
paras.zh: 新研究的涌现给这个问题带来了新的紧迫性：人工智能如何改变数学发现？在争夺引人注目的突破的竞赛中，人工智能公司通常不会透露他们的方法和数据。人工智能公司之间的竞争可能会压倒人类的协作和理解。

paras.en: This tension had been playing out in miniature on a website Bloom runs that tracks progress on more than 1,000 problems originally posed and collected by Paul Erdős, one of the 20th century’s most prolific mathematicians. Here, people used to collaborate to discuss open problems, or ones for which the best solution either hasn’t been found or isn’t known to the greater math community. But increasingly, visitors were competing to close open problems with AI proofs that they often didn’t understand. Bloom, a mathematician at the University of Manchester in England, doesn’t want to spend his days refereeing AI-generated work. So, soon after we spoke, and before he knew that OpenAI would be announcing its latest results, Bloom posted that he’d no longer tag problems as open or solved, and he also closed comments.
paras.zh: 这种紧张局势在布鲁姆运营的一个网站上得到了缩影，该网站跟踪了 20 世纪最多产的数学家之一保罗·埃尔多斯 (Paul Erdős) 最初提出和收集的 1000 多个问题的进展情况。在这里，人们过去常常合作讨论未解决的问题，或者尚未找到或不为更大的数学界所知的最佳解决方案的问题。但越来越多的访问者竞相用他们通常不理解的人工智能证明来解决未解决的问题。布鲁姆是英国曼彻斯特大学的数学家，他不想把时间花在评审人工智能生成的工作上。因此，在我们交谈后不久，在他知道 OpenAI 将宣布其最新结果之前，Bloom 发帖表示，他不会再将问题标记为“开放”或“已解决”，并且他还关闭了评论。

paras.en: It’s definitely exciting that AI can tackle so many open problems so quickly. But can it help mathematicians understand the answers and build on them?
paras.zh: 人工智能能够如此迅速地解决如此多的开放性问题，这绝对令人兴奋。但它能帮助数学家理解答案并以此为基础吗？

paras.en: Just two days after OpenAI’s deluge of results, the peer-reviewed edition of a Google DeepMind study became public. First reported in a preprint earlier this year, it offers an inside look at how one AI system tackles open math problems. The system called AlphaProof Nexus solved 9 Erdős problems and made a number of other interesting mathematical advances, researchers report October 8 in Science.
paras.zh: 就在 OpenAI 发布大量结果两天后，谷歌 DeepMind 研究的同行评审版就公开了。它于今年早些时候在预印本中首次报道，它提供了人工智能系统如何解决开放数学问题的内部视角。研究人员 10 月 8 日在《科学》杂志上报道称，这个名为 AlphaProof Nexus 的系统解决了 9 个 Erdős 问题，并取得了许多其他有趣的数学进展。

paras.en: The report includes a detailed description of how the results were obtained. Plus, human mathematicians vetted many of the proofs. That’s “quite different” from how OpenAI and Anthropic are handling their math results, Bloom says.
paras.zh: 该报告详细描述了如何获得结果。另外，人类数学家审查了许多证明。布鲁姆说，这与 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 处理数学结果的方式“完全不同”。

paras.en: “The ultimate objective of any AI for math research,” says research scientist and study co-author Swarat Chaudhuri of Google DeepMind in London, should be “to advance mathematics as done by human mathematicians.”
paras.zh: 伦敦谷歌 DeepMind 的研究科学家兼研究合著者斯瓦拉特·乔杜里 (Swarat Chaudhuri) 表示：“任何人工智能用于数学研究的最终目标都应该是“像人类数学家一样推进数学发展”。

paras.en: In the recently published study Chaudhuri and his colleagues tested different configurations of their system. To tackle a collection of 353 open Erdős problems, they used multiple agents powered by the Gemini language model. These could call on AlphaProof, an AI model specially trained to do math, and the inspiration for the name of the overall system, for difficult steps. The agents also relied on Lean, math software that identifies steps that remain unproven, to check their logic. The agents shared their work, circulating promising proof attempts and discarding ones that weren’t going well.
paras.zh: 在最近发表的研究中，Chaudhuri 和他的同事测试了他们系统的不同配置。为了解决 353 个开放式 Erdős 问题，他们使用了由 Gemini 语言模型支持的多个代理。这些可以调用 AlphaProof，一种专门训练用于数学计算的人工智能模型，以及整个系统名称的灵感，以解决困难的步骤。特工们还依靠精益数学软件来识别尚未证实的步骤，以检查他们的逻辑。特工们分享了他们的工作，传播有希望的证明尝试，并放弃那些进展不顺利的尝试。

paras.en: The team also tested a simpler setup on the nine problems the full system solved. Independent Gemini agents worked through proofs using Lean’s feedback, without sharing attempts or consulting AlphaProof. That setup solved all nine, too. It was cheaper—using fewer computing resources—than the full system on easy problems and more expensive on the two toughest ones. The team did not establish whether the simpler setup would solve any of the problems the full system had missed.
paras.zh: 该团队还针对整个系统解决的九个问题测试了更简单的设置。独立的 Gemini 代理使用 Lean 的反馈完成了证明，没有分享尝试或咨询 AlphaProof。该设置也解决了所有九个问题。对于简单的问题，它比完整的系统更便宜（使用更少的计算资源），而对于两个最棘手的问题则更昂贵。该团队尚未确定更简单的设置是否可以解决整个系统遗漏的任何问题。

paras.en: The fact that the simpler setup could solve the same nine problems as the full system surprised Chaudhuri. It suggests that increasingly capable language models can tackle research mathematics with relatively simple checking tools.
paras.zh: 事实上，更简单的设置可以解决与完整系统相同的九个问题，这让 Chaudhuri 感到惊讶。它表明功能日益强大的语言模型可以使用相对简单的检查工具来解决研究数学问题。

paras.en: But computer-checking comes with a caveat. Lean checks only the statement it’s given, as it is written in its code. And a mathematical statement may be incorrectly translated to or from Lean code. An October 6 preprint shows why this translation matters. In the paper, the researchers pinpoint mismatches between parts of OpenAI’s written Navier–Stokes proof and its Lean counterpart. The mismatches do not mean the written proof is wrong, the team writes, but they note that a valid Lean proof does not automatically validate an AI-generated math paper.
paras.zh: 但计算机检查有一个警告。精益仅检查其给出的语句，正如其代码中所写的那样。数学陈述可能会被错误地翻译成精益代码或从精益代码中翻译出来。 10 月 6 日的预印本说明了此翻译的重要性。在论文中，研究人员查明了 OpenAI 书面的纳维-斯托克斯证明与其精益对应部分之间的不匹配之处。该团队写道，不匹配并不意味着书面证明是错误的，但他们指出，有效的精益证明不会自动验证人工智能生成的数学论文。

paras.en: That’s why the vetting human mathematicians did for the DeepMind publication is so important. “The human mathematician has to really think through the problem and set goals for the system,” Chaudhuri says. And even if the system failed to finish a proof, its checked steps helped mathematicians focus on the remaining gaps. “Math is ultimately a human art,” Chaudhuri says. “The system enhances the human user’s insights, and the human user is able to guide the system with new ideas.”
paras.zh: 这就是为什么人类数学家为 DeepMind 出版物所做的审查如此重要。 “人类数学家必须真正思考问题并为系统设定目标，”乔胡里说。即使系统未能完成证明，其检查步骤也可以帮助数学家专注于剩余的空白。 “数学归根结底是一门人类艺术，”乔胡里说。 “该系统增强了人类用户的洞察力，并且人类用户能够用新的想法来指导系统。”

paras.en: The mathematical results that the AlphaProof Nexus system achieved are “not really at the top level of importance,” says Bloom, who wasn’t involved with the work. But that underscores the team’s more measured approach. Google DeepMind, he says, is “trying to be more responsible with the science,” while companies like OpenAI are using math to showcase their software. OpenAI’s papers and accompanying Lean proofs were entirely AI-generated, leaving it up to the math community to work out what’s useful or useless.
paras.zh: 未参与这项工作的 Bloom 表示，AlphaProof Nexus 系统取得的数学结果“并不是真正重要的”。但这凸显了该团队更加谨慎的方法。他说，谷歌 DeepMind 正在“努力对科学更加负责”，而 OpenAI 等公司正在使用数学来展示他们的软件。 OpenAI 的论文和随附的精益证明完全由人工智能生成，由数学界来决定什么有用或无用。

paras.en: OpenAI says they worked with an independent advisory group to develop best practices on how to share their AI math results. But that group has said their advice was to not test unreleased AI models on advanced math, guidance the company clearly ignored.
paras.zh: OpenAI 表示，他们与一个独立咨询小组合作，开发了如何分享人工智能数学结果的最佳实践。但该组织表示，他们的建议是不要在高等数学上测试未发布的人工智能模型，而该公司显然忽视了这一指导。

paras.en: The company’s fast-moving, competitive approach continues to alienate mathematicians such as Bryna Kra of Northwestern University in Evanston, Ill. She says the company made some improvements in their efforts to cite past literature. And she’s excited about AI’s potential to solve important problems in math. But there is widespread concern, she says, that AI models have accessed people’s unpublished work. “We had a healthy, collaborative, sharing culture that is being destroyed,” she says. “Now, people are wary of sharing their ideas.”
paras.zh: 该公司快速发展、竞争性的做法继续疏远了伊利诺伊州埃文斯顿西北大学的 Bryna Kra 等数学家。她表示，该公司在引用过去文献方面做出了一些改进。她对人工智能解决重要数学问题的潜力感到兴奋。但她表示，人们普遍担心人工智能模型已经获取了人们未发表的作品。 “我们拥有健康、协作、分享的文化，但现在正在被破坏，”她说。 “现在，人们对分享自己的想法持谨慎态度。”

paras.en: Not all mathematicians feel this way about AI. The technology is “making math more accessible,” says Andrew Turner, who wonders why a small group of mathematicians should get to decide how we solve problems. Turner, who studied math and physics and is Now CTO of the company Plasma AI, based in New York City thinks “math is becoming engineering.” And doing math with machines will allow people to “answer questions previously unfathomable.”
paras.zh: 并非所有数学家都对人工智能有这样的看法。安德鲁·特纳说，这项技术“让数学变得更容易理解”，他想知道为什么一小群数学家应该决定我们如何解决问题。特纳学习了数学和物理，现任纽约 Plasma AI 公司的首席技术官，他认为“数学正在成为工程学”。用机器做数学将使人们能够“回答以前难以理解的问题”。

paras.en: A few days after Bloom shut down the competition on his website, Plasma AI announced a new website to track progress on Erdős problems. They will welcome AI results.
paras.zh: Bloom 关闭其网站上的竞赛几天后，Plasma AI 宣布建立一个新网站来跟踪 Erdős 问题的进展情况。他们会欢迎人工智能的结果。

paras.en: Bloom doesn’t see math as a Silicon Valley–esque move-fast-and-break-things competition. I agree, and hope that curious people will continue to explore problems they care about, with AI helping rather than taking over. At the end of his post announcing the changes to his website, Bloom wrote something that makes me tear up every time I read it. I hope everyone, even the most enthusiastic AI users, can find the time for this type of work: “Be confused, be stuck, be inspired. Find a messy proof, then find a better one,” he wrote. “Get tired, get hungry, get into a flow state. Argue, laugh, give up, drink some coffee and attack it again. Be human. Let your brain be open.”
paras.zh: 布鲁姆并不认为数学是硅谷式的快速行动、打破常规的竞赛。我同意，并希望好奇的人们能够继续探索他们关心的问题，让人工智能提供帮助而不是接管。在他宣布网站发生变化的帖子的最后，布鲁姆写了一些让我每次读到都会流泪的东西。我希望每个人，甚至是最热情的人工智能用户，都能找到时间进行此类工作：“感到困惑，陷入困境，受到启发。找到一个混乱的证明，然后找到一个更好的证明，”他写道。 “累了，饿了，进入心流状态。争论，大笑，放弃，喝点咖啡，然后再次攻击它。做人。让你的大脑开放。”

articles.title: A Major Superconductor 'Speed Limit' Was Just Broken
articles.author: Ivan Farkas

paras.en: Superconductors give us sci-fi-worthy technologies like levitating trains, Big-Bang-replicating particle colliders, and medical machines that reveal our innermost secrets – thankfully only the physiological ones and not, perhaps, a secret love of polka dance.
paras.zh: 超导体为我们提供了科幻般的技术，比如悬浮火车、复制大爆炸的粒子对撞机，以及揭示我们内心深处秘密的医疗机器——幸运的是，只有生理秘密，而不是对波尔卡舞的秘密热爱。

paras.en: But superconducting states are fragile. Materials must be cooled to very low temperatures, approaching the dark frigidity of outer space, to conduct electricity without resistance and subsequent energy loss.
paras.zh: 但超导态是脆弱的。材料必须冷却到非常低的温度，接近外层空间的黑暗寒冷，才能在没有电阻和随后的能量损失的情况下导电。

paras.en: The strength of the electrical current and of external magnetic fields can also snap these materials out of their superconducting states, as a curious cat's whisker or mistimed sneeze can knock down a precarious series of dominos.
paras.zh: 电流和外部磁场的强度也可以使这些材料脱离超导状态，就像好奇的猫的胡须或不合时宜的喷嚏可以推倒一系列不稳定的多米诺骨牌一样。

paras.en: Yet there's an even higher limit that's difficult to measure via conventional means, like direct current (DC) transport, because it's preempted by quantum disruptions that occur in just billionths of a second.
paras.zh: 然而，还有一个更高的限制很难通过传统手段（例如直流（DC）传输）来测量，因为它被仅十亿分之一秒内发生的量子中断所抢占。

paras.en: This is the depairing limit, where the entangled pairs of electrons, called Cooper pairs, that yield superconductivity are ripped apart.
paras.zh: 这是解对极限，在该极限中，产生超导性的纠缠电子对（称为库珀对）被撕裂。

paras.en: But in a breakthrough study published in Nature Physics, researchers smashed a superconductor 'speed limit' to probe this depairing, zipping past the disruptive quantum processes like a Formula 1 racer zooming past a Model T with a wonky wheel.
paras.zh: 但在《自然物理学》杂志上发表的一项突破性研究中，研究人员突破了超导体的“速度限制”来探索这种配对，快速穿过破坏性的量子过程，就像一级方程式赛车手从车轮摇晃的 T 型车上疾驰而过一样。

paras.en: Unlike type I superconductors, which are generally pure metals and not so technologically useful due to their especially fragile magnetic limits, type II superconductors comprise a physical compromise:
paras.zh: 与 I 型超导体不同，I 型超导体通常是纯金属，由于其特别脆弱的磁极限而在技术上不太有用，II 型超导体包含物理妥协：

paras.en: They have higher magnetic thresholds because they allow internal magnetic fields to propagate as tiny tornadoes of electricity, called quantum vortices, keeping them in a superconducting state in more extreme conditions.
paras.zh: 它们具有更高的磁阈值，因为它们允许内部磁场以微小的电龙卷风（称为量子涡旋）的形式传播，从而使它们在更极端的条件下保持超导状态。

paras.en: However, when an electric current running through a type II material becomes too strong, it whips up the tiny tornadoes, causing them to move, generating resistance and heat that stops superconductivity.
paras.zh: 然而，当流过 II 型材料的电流变得太强时，它会激起微小的龙卷风，导致它们移动，产生电阻和热量，从而阻止超导性。

paras.en: "Our strategy was to outrun the vortex dynamics," conceptualizes lead author Eryin Wang, a physicist at the Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter (MPSD) in Hamburg, Germany.
paras.zh: “我们的策略是超越涡流动力学，”主要作者、德国汉堡马克斯·普朗克物质结构与动力学研究所 (MPSD) 的物理学家 Eryin Wang 概念化道。

paras.en: The researchers compared two superconducting materials, including niobium nitride (NbN) and a member of the yttrium barium copper oxide (YBCO) family of superconductors that exhibit 'high-temperature superconductivity'.
paras.zh: 研究人员比较了两种超导材料，包括氮化铌（NbN）和具有“高温超导性”的超导体钇钡铜氧化物（YBCO）家族成员。

paras.en: They chose these materials because the former has an s-wave gap symmetry and the latter has a d-wave gap symmetry. This property dictate how easy it is to rip apart their paired electrons and therefore snap them out of their superconductive states.
paras.zh: 他们选择这些材料是因为前者具有 s 波间隙对称性，后者具有 d 波间隙对称性。这一特性决定了撕裂成对电子并使其脱离超导状态的容易程度。

paras.en: But how does one outrun quantum processes, which exist at the limits of physics? By developing an optical-electric circuit that outpaces the velocity of the vortices – which act at tens of kilometers per second – by multiple orders of magnitude.
paras.zh: 但是，如何超越存在于物理极限的量子过程呢？通过开发一种光电电路，其速度超过涡流的速度（每秒数十公里）多个数量级。

paras.en: This setup shot ultra-quick laser pulses of green light lasting just 300 femtoseconds, or quadrillionths of a second, at a switch that turned the optical laser pulse into an electric current pulse that lasted picoseconds, or trillionths of a second (a relative slowpoke in comparison).
paras.zh: 该装置发射了仅持续 300 飞秒（即万亿分之一秒）的超快绿光激光脉冲，开关将光学激光脉冲转变为持续皮秒（即万亿分之一秒）的电流脉冲（相比之下，速度相对较慢）。

paras.en: This is much quicker than the vortex dynamics could cause resistance and heat and the loss of superconductivity.
paras.zh: 这比涡旋动力学可能导致电阻和热量以及超导性损失要快得多。

paras.en: In other words, a real quantum tortoise and hare situation, but one in which the hare is off the starting blocks while the tortoise is still having breakfast (perhaps the fox judging the contest was surreptitiously slipped a few eggs to overlook this 'inconsistency').
paras.zh: 换句话说，这是一种真正的量子乌龟和兔子的情况，但兔子已经离开了起跑器，而乌龟仍在吃早餐（也许评判比赛的狐狸偷偷地扔了一些鸡蛋来忽略这种“不一致”）。

paras.en: "Our results suggest that picosecond transport can provide access to microscopic properties of superconductors, including their gap symmetry, that are not directly available from conventional DC transport," explains Andrea Cavalleri, leader of the Condensed Matter Dynamics group at MPSD.
paras.zh: MPSD 凝聚态动力学小组负责人 Andrea Cavalleri 解释说：“我们的结果表明，皮秒输运可以提供超导体的微观特性，包括其间隙对称性，而这些特性是传统直流输运无法直接获得的。”

paras.en: Specifically, the NbN retained its superconductive state until the applied electric current reached a well-defined threshold, the researchers note, which is well above the conventional DC output because it's of such a short duration. At this point, its Cooper pairs fell apart and its superconductivity abruptly stopped.
paras.zh: 研究人员指出，具体来说，NbN 保持其超导状态，直到施加的电流达到明确的阈值，该阈值远高于传统的直流输出，因为它的持续时间很短。此时，它的库珀对解体了，它的超导性突然停止了。

paras.en: The YBCO material, on the other hand, displayed a gradual weakening of its superconductive state. This difference arises due to their different gap symmetries.
paras.zh: 另一方面，YBCO 材料的超导状态逐渐减弱。这种差异是由于它们不同的间隙对称性而产生的。

paras.en: The s-wave of the NbN has an energy gap (the energy needed to disentangle Cooper pairs) that's the same in all directions of momentum space.
paras.zh: NbN 的 s 波具有在动量空间所有方向上相同的能隙（解开库珀对所需的能量）。

paras.en: But in YBCO, the energy gap varies significantly and even disappears in certain directions of momentum space.
paras.zh: 但在YBCO中，能隙在动量空间的某些方向上变化很大，甚至消失。

paras.en: In other words, the former goes all-in on one poker hand, while the other may prefer to lose its money more slowly.
paras.zh: 换句话说，前者在一手牌上全押，而另一手牌可能更愿意更慢地输钱。

paras.en: The researchers thus got to the very fundamental root of superconduction, the stability of a material's Cooper pairs, the core quantum concept whence other effects emerge.
paras.zh: 研究人员因此找到了超导的根本根源，即材料库珀对的稳定性，这是产生其他效应的核心量子概念。

paras.en: The "novel approach" presented herein offers a framework for testing the key properties of superconducting materials, and thus 'zapping' a greater variety of superconductors can reveal properties like gap symmetries and how the materials react on their fundamental timescales.
paras.zh: 本文提出的“新方法”提供了一个测试超导材料关键特性的框架，因此“改变”更多种类的超导体可以揭示诸如间隙对称性以及材料在其基本时间尺度上如何反应等特性。

paras.en: As summarized by Jianqiao Meng, a professor of physics at Central South University, who was not involved in this work, sometimes the race really does go to the swift:
paras.zh: 正如未参与这项工作的中南大学物理学教授孟建桥所总结的那样，有时比赛确实会胜出：

paras.en: "This work highlights the potential of ultrafast current pulses as a powerful new tool for accessing intrinsic superconducting properties."
paras.zh: “这项工作凸显了超快电流脉冲作为获取固有超导特性的强大新工具的潜力。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Nature Physics.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《自然物理学》上。

articles.title: Study Shows Meat Eaters Are More Likely to Survive to 100, But There's a Catch
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: Humans are living longer than ever before. By 2050, scientists predict that nearly half a billion people could be older than 80.
paras.zh: 人类的寿命比以往任何时候都长。科学家预测，到 2050 年，将有近 5 亿人年龄超过 80 岁。

paras.en: The rise in human life expectancy is partly due to improvements in nutrition, but which food choices lead to the longest and healthiest outcomes in older age?
paras.zh: 人类预期寿命的延长部分归因于营养的改善，但哪些食物选择可以带来最长、最健康的老年结果呢？

paras.en: Scientists are still trying to figure that out.
paras.zh: 科学家们仍在试图弄清楚这一点。

paras.en: In younger cohorts, some particular diets are associated with years of added life, especially those focused on whole, plant-based foods and healthy fats.
paras.zh: 在年轻群体中，一些特定的饮食与延长寿命有关，尤其是那些注重天然植物性食品和健康脂肪的饮食。

paras.en: But meat choices are more controversial, and they typically come with a catch.
paras.zh: 但肉类的选择更具争议性，而且通常会带来一些问题。

paras.en: A study from China has now added another wrinkle to the research. Among more than 5,000 people aged 80 and over, researchers found that female meat eaters were more likely to reach age 100 than female vegetarians.
paras.zh: 来自中国的一项研究为这项研究增添了另一个难题。研究人员在 5000 多名 80 岁及以上老人中发现，肉食女性比素食女性更有可能活到 100 岁。

paras.en: There was no significant association between longevity and vegetarianism among males when the researchers analyzed the data by sex.
paras.zh: 当研究人员按性别分析数据时，男性的长寿和素食主义之间没有显着关联。

paras.en: Before you go sending this article to every female vegetarian you know, you should stay for the nuance.
paras.zh: 在您将这篇文章发送给您认识的每一位女性素食主义者之前，您应该留心其中的细微差别。

paras.en: It was only vegetarian participants deemed underweight who were less likely to live to 100 than meat eaters.
paras.zh: 只有被认为体重过轻的素食参与者比肉食者活到 100 岁的可能性更小。

paras.en: "Daily consumption of meat was associated with a 44 percent higher likelihood of reaching 100 years old [compared to a vegetarian diet] in the underweight group, whereas this association did not present in the normal weight or overweight group," the study authors conclude.
paras.zh: 研究作者总结道：“在体重不足的人群中，每天吃肉与吃素的人活到 100 岁的可能性高出 44% 相关，而在正常体重或超重的人群中，这种关联并不存在。”

paras.en: What's more, vegetarians who ate fish, dairy, or eggs had a similar chance of reaching 100 as meat eaters.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，吃鱼、奶制品或鸡蛋的素食者与肉食者达到 100 的几率相似。

paras.en: This suggests that older female adults who eat enough calories and essential nutrients may increase their odds of becoming a centenarian.
paras.zh: 这表明，摄入足够热量和必需营养素的老年女性可能会增加成为百岁老人的几率。

paras.en: The findings support recent research that suggests protecting muscle mass by eating protein is vital to healthy aging.
paras.zh: 这些发现支持了最近的研究，即通过摄入蛋白质来保护肌肉质量对于健康衰老至关重要。

paras.en: The new data come from one of the largest studies on older adults anywhere in the world: the Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey (CLHLS).
paras.zh: 新数据来自世界上最大的老年人研究之一：中国纵向健康长寿调查（CLHLS）。

paras.en: Researchers at Fudan University, the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention, and Shanghai Jiao Tong University compared the outcomes of 1,459 centenarians with those of 3,744 non-centenarians in their 80s and 90s.
paras.zh: 复旦大学、中国疾病预防控制中心和上海交通大学的研究人员对 1,459 名百岁老人与 3,744 名 80 岁和 90 岁的非百岁老人的结果进行了比较。

paras.en: The team found that body mass index (BMI) partly explained the association between vegetarianism and shorter life expectancy.
paras.zh: 研究小组发现，体重指数（BMI）在一定程度上解释了素食主义与较短预期寿命之间的关联。

paras.en: Given that older populations are more likely to be underweight, the authors suggest that the role of BMI in longevity is "worth exploring" further.
paras.zh: 鉴于老年人群更有可能体重不足，作者认为体重指数在长寿中的作用“值得进一步探讨”。

paras.en: The "obesity paradox", for instance, is a term that describes how more body weight seems to be associated with better health outcomes in older populations. This is the opposite of what is found in younger populations.
paras.zh: 例如，“肥胖悖论”这个术语描述了老年人群中体重增加与更好的健康结果之间的关系。这与年轻人中的情况相反。

paras.en: The centenarian study in China can only reveal associations, which means it's possible that other factors are impacting the results.
paras.zh: 中国的百岁老人研究只能揭示关联性，这意味着其他因素可能会影响结果。

paras.en: The study, for instance, doesn't account for how eating habits might change over time; the surveys only assessed what participants ate in their later years, and that may be influenced by how easy the foods are to chew.
paras.zh: 例如，这项研究并没有考虑饮食习惯如何随着时间的推移而改变。这些调查仅评估了参与者晚年吃的东西，这可能会受到食物咀嚼容易程度的影响。

paras.en: Previous research, however, supports the idea that lifestyle choices, such as diet, could be major reasons why some people live to 100.
paras.zh: 然而，之前的研究支持这样一种观点，即饮食等生活方式的选择可能是某些人活到 100 岁的主要原因。

paras.en: In fact, by some estimates, reaching age 90 can be explained by 70 percent healthy behaviors, such as sleep, physical activity, or diet.
paras.zh: 事实上，根据一些估计，70% 的健康行为可以解释 70% 的人能活到 90 岁，例如睡眠、体力活动或饮食。

paras.en: It's possible that older adults may have different nutritional needs, yet many studies on vegetarianism focus on younger cohorts.
paras.zh: 老年人可能有不同的营养需求，但许多关于素食主义的研究都集中在年轻人身上。

paras.en: One study of more than 65,000 people, young and old, found that those who eat a vegetarian diet may face a higher risk of fractures, possibly due to lower calcium and protein intake.
paras.zh: 一项针对超过 65,000 名年轻人和老年人的研究发现，吃素食的人可能面临更高的骨折风险，这可能是由于钙和蛋白质摄入量较低所致。

paras.en: Though that's not entirely settled either – a 2026 review from University of Wisconsin-Madison researchers argued the opposite case, that lower protein intake may actually support healthier aging in several organisms, possibly because high-protein diets can keep cells locked in a constant growth mode. Exactly how much protein older adults need remains a live debate.
paras.zh: 尽管这个问题还没有完全解决——威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校研究人员在 2026 年发表的一篇评论提出了相反的观点，即较低的蛋白质摄入量实际上可能支持多种生物体更健康的衰老，可能是因为高蛋白饮食可以使细胞保持恒定的生长模式。老年人到底需要多少蛋白质仍然是一个争论不休的话题。

paras.en: Nutrition, however, is an extremely complex area of research, and health outcomes can be influenced by a plethora of societal, environmental, and individual factors.
paras.zh: 然而，营养是一个极其复杂的研究领域，健康结果可能受到多种社会、环境和个人因素的影响。

paras.en: In all probability, the best food choices for extending life require diversity and balance, differing from person to person.
paras.zh: 很可能，延长寿命的最佳食物选择需要多样性和平衡，因人而异。

paras.en: Vegetarian diets, plant-based diets, and low-meat diets have been linked to lower risks of certain health issues, such as heart disease, stroke, type 2 diabetes, and obesity.
paras.zh: 素食、植物性饮食和低肉饮食与降低某些健康问题的风险有关，如心脏病、中风、2 型糖尿病和肥胖。

paras.en: Still, not all meat is equally associated with negative health outcomes, and the amount can matter. Processed meats and red meat, for instance, are often linked to poorer health and shorter longevity, which is why they are generally recommended to be eaten in moderation.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，并非所有肉类都与负面健康结果同等相关，而且肉类的数量也很重要。例如，加工肉类和红肉通常与健康状况不佳和寿命较短​​有关，这就是为什么通常建议适量食用它们。

paras.en: Related: Study Reveals a Turning Point When Your Body's Aging Accelerates
paras.zh: 相关：研究揭示了身体加速衰老的转折点

paras.en: "Our findings emphasized the importance of a balanced diet from both animal- and plant-derived food for healthy longevity," write the team.
paras.zh: 研究小组写道：“我们的研究结果强调了动物性和植物性食品的均衡饮食对于健康长寿的重要性。”

paras.en: "Future studies focusing on older adults of advanced age are needed for the formulation of dietary guidance."
paras.zh: “未来需要针对高龄老年人进行研究，以制定饮食指导。”

paras.en: The study was published in The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition.
paras.zh: 该研究发表在《美国临床营养学杂志》上。

articles.title: Ending Clock Changes? Health Experts Say There's a Winner Between Standard And Daylight Saving Time
articles.author: Esra Öz

paras.en: Keeping the clocks on summer time all year means lighter evenings, but it also delays winter sunrise by an hour on the clock. People getting up early for work or school spend more of the morning in darkness.
paras.zh: 全年将时钟保持在夏季时间意味着夜晚会更明亮，但也会使冬季日出时间延迟一个小时。人们早起去上班或上学，早上的大部分时间都在黑暗中度过。

paras.en: A new Canadian analysis concludes that permanent standard time is the better choice for health if seasonal clock changes are abolished, because it preserves earlier access to morning light.
paras.zh: 加拿大的一项新分析得出的结论是，如果废除季节性时钟变化，永久标准时间对健康来说是更好的选择，因为它可以保留较早的晨光。

paras.en: British Columbia adopted permanent daylight saving time in March. Alberta and the Northwest Territories have also adopted year-round daylight saving time and will skip the November clock change. In the US, the House passed a bill to make daylight saving time permanent on July 14, and it was referred to a Senate committee the following day.
paras.zh: 不列颠哥伦比亚省于三月采用永久夏令时。艾伯塔省和西北地区也采用了全年夏令时，并将跳过 11 月份的时钟变化。在美国，众议院于 7 月 14 日通过了一项永久实行夏令时的法案，并于第二天提交给参议院委员会。

paras.en: Psychiatrist Raymond Lam of the University of British Columbia and his colleagues assessed the health consequences of the two options: standard time, usually observed in winter, and daylight saving time, which runs an hour ahead.
paras.zh: 不列颠哥伦比亚大学的精神病学家雷蒙德·林（Raymond Lam）和他的同事评估了两种选择的健康后果：标准时间（通常在冬季）和夏令时（提前一小时）。

paras.en: Sleep and circadian rhythms researcher Ralph Mistlberger of Simon Fraser University co-authored the peer-reviewed analysis, which reviewed published research on biological rhythms, sleep, mood, education, and economic effects. The team also examined countries' experiences with permanent time policies and compared sunrise and sunset times across Canadian cities.
paras.zh: 西蒙弗雷泽大学的睡眠和昼夜节律研究员拉尔夫·米斯特伯格 (Ralph Mistlberger) 共同撰写了这份同行评审的分析报告，该分析回顾了已发表的有关生物节律、睡眠、情绪、教育和经济影响的研究。该团队还研究了各国在永久时间政策方面的经验，并比较了加拿大各城市的日出和日落时间。

paras.en: In Toronto, the latest winter sunrise, in early January, would come at 7:51 am under permanent standard time and 8:51 am under permanent daylight saving time.
paras.zh: 在多伦多，最晚的冬季日出时间为 1 月初，永久标准时间为上午 7:51，永久夏令时为上午 8:51。

paras.en: A Toronto resident waking at 7 am in early January would get up before sunrise under either setting, but daylight would arrive an hour sooner under standard time. Neither option changes the length of the day.
paras.zh: 在任何一种情况下，一月初早上 7 点起床的多伦多居民都会在日出前起床，但在标准时间下，日出会提前一个小时。这两个选项都不会改变一天的长度。

paras.en: The brain's main circadian clock coordinates sleep, alertness, and other daily functions. It needs daily adjustment to stay in step with the day. Morning light helps move it earlier, while evening light pushes it later.
paras.zh: 大脑的主要生物钟协调睡眠、警觉性和其他日常功能。它需要每天进行调整才能与时俱进。晨光有助于将其提前移动，而傍晚的光线则将其推得较晚。

paras.en: "Imagine a wristwatch that runs 10 minutes slow each day, and every morning you make the 10 minute correction by setting it forward," Mistlberger explained to ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: Mistlberger 向 ScienceAlert 解释道：“想象一下，一只手表每天走慢 10 分钟，每天早上你都可以通过将其向前拨动来进行 10 分钟的校正。”

paras.en: With less morning light, sleep rhythms can slip later while school and work still begin at the same hour. Getting up on time may mean cutting sleep short.
paras.zh: 由于早晨光线较少，睡眠节奏可能会变晚，而学校和工作仍会在同一时间开始。准时起床可能意味着缩短睡眠时间。

paras.en: Social jetlag, the gap between the body clock and school or work schedules, has been linked to poorer physical and mental health, as has insufficient sleep. Seasonal clock changes can also disrupt sleep.
paras.zh: 社交时差，即生物钟与学校或工作时间之间的差距，与睡眠不足一样，与较差的身心健康有关。季节的时钟变化也会扰乱睡眠。

paras.en: The analysis also draws on geographic comparisons: people living farther west within a time zone get later sunrises by the clock. Studies have linked this position with shorter sleep and some poorer health and economic outcomes, though these associations do not prove causation.
paras.zh: 该分析还利用了地理比较：居住在某个时区内较西边的人们，日出时间较晚。研究已将这种姿势与较短的睡眠以及一些较差的健康和经济结果联系起来，尽管这些关联并不能证明因果关系。

paras.en: The researchers considered seasonal affective disorder, a form of depression often experienced in winter. One leading explanation involves the body clock slipping later when morning light is delayed. Morning bright-light therapy helps move it earlier; a later sunrise on the clock works in the opposite direction.
paras.zh: 研究人员考虑了季节性情感障碍，这是一种在冬季经常出现的抑郁症。一种主要的解释是，当晨光延迟时，生物钟就会变慢。早晨的强光疗法有助于提早移动；时钟上较晚的日出以相反的方向运行。

paras.en: Teenagers and young adults may be especially vulnerable because their body clocks naturally shift later at that age.
paras.zh: 青少年和年轻人可能特别容易受到伤害，因为他们的生物钟在这个年龄段自然会变晚。

paras.en: "Later school and work times would help," Mistlberger said. Brighter indoor lighting in the morning could also help, he added.
paras.zh: “推迟上学和工作时间会有所帮助，”米斯特伯格说。他补充说，早上更明亮的室内照明也会有所帮助。

paras.en: Several countries have tried year-round daylight saving time before. The US introduced it in 1974 and abandoned it within the year, following concerns about dark winter mornings and children traveling to school before sunrise. Russia adopted it in 2011 and reversed it in 2014.
paras.zh: 一些国家此前曾尝试过全年夏令时。美国于 1974 年引入该制度，但出于对黑暗的冬季早晨和儿童在日出前上学的担忧，一年内就放弃了该制度。俄罗斯于2011年采用该法案，并于2014年撤销。

paras.en: Permanent daylight saving time would keep evenings lighter, allowing more time for outdoor activity and socializing. Standard time brings earlier winter dusk, while early summer sunrise may wake some people too early. Latitude and location within time zones also determine how much the choice matters in a given place.
paras.zh: 永久夏令时将使夜晚变得更加明亮，从而有更多时间进行户外活动和社交。标准时间带来了更早的冬季黄昏，而初夏的日出可能会过早地唤醒一些人。时区内的纬度和位置也决定了选择在特定地点的重要性。

paras.en: Much of the evidence comes from observational research and geographic comparisons, leaving uncertainty about permanent policies' long-term health consequences.
paras.zh: 大部分证据来自观察性研究和地理比较，这使得永久性政策对健康的长期影响存在不确定性。

paras.en: The researchers recommend permanent standard time. If governments choose year-round daylight saving time, they advise considering later school and work starts, improving morning light exposure, and tracking whether sleep problems, winter depression, absenteeism, and road injuries rise.
paras.zh: 研究人员推荐永久标准时间。如果政府选择全年夏令时，他们建议考虑推迟上学和上班时间，改善早晨的光照，并跟踪睡眠问题、冬季抑郁、缺勤和道路伤害是否增加。

paras.en: The research has been published in Canadian Medical Association Journal.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《加拿大医学会杂志》上。

articles.title: The secret to easier exercise as an adult may start in childhood

paras.en: The secret to easier exercise as an adult may start in childhood
paras.zh: 成年人更轻松锻炼的秘诀可能从童年开始

paras.en: A surprising new study suggests that staying active while growing up could make exercise easier and less exhausting for the rest of your life.
paras.zh: 一项令人惊讶的新研究表明，在成长过程中保持活跃可以让你在余生中更轻松地锻炼，减少疲劳。

paras.en: - Exercise during childhood could have a surprising lifelong benefit, potentially making physical activity less exhausting in adulthood. In a study involving guinea fowl, researchers discovered that birds accustomed to carrying weights while growing up could carry those weights as adults without using extra energy, while untrained birds burned 23% more.
paras.zh: - 童年时期的锻炼可能会带来令人惊讶的终生益处，有可能使成年后的体力活动不再那么疲惫。在一项涉及珍珠鸡的研究中，研究人员发现，习惯于在成长过程中负重的鸟类在成年后可以在不消耗额外能量的情况下负重，而未经训练的鸟类燃烧的热量多出 23%。

paras.en: How much energy your body needs to move as an adult could be influenced by how active you were during childhood. A new study led by researchers at Penn State suggests that physical activity early in life may have lasting effects on movement efficiency. Using birds as a model, the scientists provided the first direct evidence that experiences during development can change how much energy animals expend when moving as adults.
paras.zh: 作为一个成年人，你的身体运动所需的能量可能会受到你童年时期的活跃程度的影响。宾夕法尼亚州立大学研究人员领导的一项新研究表明，生命早期的身体活动可能对运动效率产生持久影响。科学家们以鸟类为模型，提供了第一个直接证据，证明发育过程中的经历可以改变动物成年后运动时消耗的能量。

paras.en: According to Jonas Rubenson, a professor of kinesiology at Penn State, the ability to move efficiently could play an important role in animal evolution. Animals that spend less energy getting around may have more resources available for essential activities such as finding food, hunting, and reproducing. The findings, published in Proceedings of the Royal Society B, Biological Sciences, suggest that the energy demands of movement are more adaptable than scientists previously believed.
paras.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州立大学运动机能学教授乔纳斯·鲁本森表示，有效移动的能力可能在动物进化中发挥重要作用。花费较少能量四处走动的动物可能有更多的资源可用于基本活动，例如寻找食物、狩猎和繁殖。发表在《英国皇家学会学报 B 生物科学》上的研究结果表明，运动的能量需求比科学家之前认为的更具适应性。

paras.en: To investigate, the researchers attached small weights to one leg of young guinea fowl, birds closely related to chickens that walk on two legs like humans. They wanted to determine whether carrying extra weight during development would change how efficiently the birds moved once they matured.
paras.zh: 为了进行研究，研究人员在幼年珍珠鸡的一条腿上安装了小重物，这种鸟类与像人类一样用两条腿行走的鸡密切相关。他们想确定在发育过程中携带额外的重量是否会改变鸟类成熟后的移动效率。

paras.en: The results revealed a striking difference. Birds that grew up carrying the weights could walk with the added load without expending additional energy. By comparison, birds raised without weights required 23% more energy when the same load was attached to their legs.
paras.zh: 结果显示出显着的差异。从小就负重长大的鸟类可以在增加的负重下行走，而无需消耗额外的能量。相比之下，当相同的负重施加到腿上时，没有负重饲养的家禽需要多 23% 的能量。

paras.en: "This study showed how limb loading -- the application of mechanical stress on arms or legs, typically through weights or exercise -- during development can help an animal save energy during movement throughout its lifespan," said Rubenson, senior author of the study. "This is one of the first studies to indicate that animals' behaviors and environments in youth can affect how effortful moving is as adults."
paras.zh: 该研究的资深作者鲁本森说：“这项研究表明，在发育过程中，肢体负荷（通常通过举重或锻炼对手臂或腿部施加机械应力）可以帮助动物在其整个生命周期的运动过程中节省能量。” “这是首批表明动物幼年时的行为和环境会影响成年后移动的费力程度的研究之一。”

paras.en: Why Childhood Exercise Could Matter for Lifelong Health
paras.zh: 为什么童年锻炼对终生健康很重要

paras.en: Although the experiment involved birds, the findings raise important questions about human physical activity. One widely accepted scientific hypothesis proposes that people tend to avoid movement when it feels physically demanding or requires substantial energy.
paras.zh: 尽管实验涉及鸟类，但研究结果提出了有关人类身体活动的重要问题。一项被广泛接受的科学假设认为，当人们感到体力消耗大或需要大量能量时，人们往往会避免运动。

paras.en: If early activity influences movement efficiency in humans as it does in these birds, people who were less active during childhood might need to expend more energy to perform the same movements as adults. That additional effort could make them less inclined to exercise, potentially reinforcing a pattern of inactivity.
paras.zh: 如果早期活动影响人类的运动效率，就像这些鸟类一样，那么童年时期不太活跃的人可能需要花费更多的能量来执行与成年人相同的运动。这种额外的努力可能会让他们不太愿意锻炼，可能会强化不活动的模式。

paras.en: Rubenson believes the discovery could have broad implications for public health, particularly as children today are generally less physically active than those in earlier generations.
paras.zh: 鲁本森认为，这一发现可能对公共健康产生广泛影响，特别是因为当今的儿童普遍比前几代人的身体活动较少。

paras.en: "Overall, children in the U.S. today are much less active than previous generations," Rubenson said. "This study suggests that more exercise through play and exercise during childhood could make it easier for people to remain or become more active as adults. If people do not need to exert as much energy to move as adults, then exercise -- and all its health benefits -- will be more accessible to them. This could have implications for many aspects of our nation's well-being, from heart health to mental health."
paras.zh: “总体而言，当今美国的儿童比前几代人活跃得多，”鲁本森说。 “这项研究表明，在童年时期通过玩耍和锻炼进行更多的锻炼可以使人们在成年后更容易保持或变得更加活跃。如果人们不需要像成年人那样消耗那么多的能量来运动，那么他们将更容易获得锻炼及其所有健康益处。这可能会对我们国家福祉的许多方面产生影响，从心脏健康到心理健康。”

paras.en: How Researchers Tested the Effects of Early Exercise
paras.zh: 研究人员如何测试早期锻炼的效果

paras.en: The experiment followed 12 guinea fowl from two weeks of age until they reached 16 weeks, when the birds were approaching their full adult size.
paras.zh: 该实验对 12 只珍珠鸡进行了跟踪调查，从两周大到 16 周，此时这些珍珠鸡已接近成年。

paras.en: Half of the birds wore lead bands on one leg, with each band weighing 4% of the bird's body weight. The remaining six birds developed without any added weight. Apart from this difference, all 12 animals experienced the same living conditions and exercise routines.
paras.zh: 一半的鸟在一条腿上佩戴了铅带，每条带的重量为鸟体重的 4%。剩下的六只鸟在没有增加任何体重的情况下发育。除了这种差异之外，所有 12 只动物的生活条件和锻炼习惯都是相同的。

paras.en: When the birds reached nine weeks of age, the researchers began training them to walk on a treadmill.
paras.zh: 当这些鸟长到九周大时，研究人员开始训练它们在跑步机上行走。

paras.en: At 16 weeks, the team assessed their energy expenditure using a flow-through metabolic chamber fitted to the treadmill. This equipment measured the oxygen each bird consumed, along with the carbon dioxide and water vapor it released. According to the researchers, this approach is considered the gold standard for determining how much energy an animal uses during a particular activity.
paras.zh: 第 16 周时，研究小组使用跑步机上安装的流通代谢室评估了他们的能量消耗。该设备测量每只鸟消耗的氧气，以及释放的二氧化碳和水蒸气。研究人员表示，这种方法被认为是确定动物在特定活动中消耗多少能量的黄金标准。

paras.en: Each bird was tested under three conditions: standing still, walking on the treadmill without added weight, and walking while wearing a weight band on one leg. By comparing oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production across these conditions, the scientists could determine how the additional load affected energy use.
paras.zh: 每只鸟都在三种条件下进行测试：静止站立、在不增加重量的情况下在跑步机上行走以及单腿佩戴负重带行走。通过比较这些条件下的耗氧量和二氧化碳产生量，科学家们可以确定额外的负荷如何影响能源使用。

paras.en: Early Training Produced a Surprising Energy-Saving Effect
paras.zh: 早期训练产生了惊人的节能效果

paras.en: The researchers found no differences in energy consumption when the birds were standing still. However, their responses changed considerably once they began walking with weights.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，当鸟儿静止不动时，能量消耗没有差异。然而，一旦他们开始负重行走，他们的反应就会发生很大变化。

paras.en: Birds that had not carried weights while growing up experienced a 23% increase in energy expenditure when walking with the added load compared with walking without it.
paras.zh: 与成长过程中没有负重的鸟类相比，在负重行走时，其能量消耗增加了 23%。

paras.en: The birds that had worn weights throughout development showed a remarkably different response. Their bodies had adapted so effectively that walking with the extra load required slightly less energy than walking without it. This unexpected result surprised the research team.
paras.zh: 在整个发育过程中承受负重的鸟类表现出截然不同的反应。他们的身体已经有效地适应了，带着额外负重行走所需的能量比不负重行走时需要的能量略少。这个意想不到的结果让研究团队感到惊讶。

paras.en: "The birds became so efficient that they were not using any more energy to carry the weight than they needed to walk without the weight," Rubenson said.
paras.zh: 鲁本森说：“这些鸟变得如此高效，以至于它们携带重量所消耗的能量并不多于它们在没有重量的情况下行走所需的能量。”

paras.en: Another unexpected finding emerged when the researchers compared the two groups. On average, birds accustomed to carrying weights throughout development used no more energy while walking with their bands than ordinary birds used when walking without any added weight.
paras.zh: 当研究人员比较两组时，出现了另一个意想不到的发现。平均而言，在整个发育过程中习惯负重的鸟类在带着带子行走时，并不比普通鸟类在没有任何额外重量的情况下行走时消耗更多的能量。

paras.en: Together, these observations suggest that experiences early in life can substantially influence how efficiently animals move as adults.
paras.zh: 总之，这些观察结果表明，生命早期的经历可以极大地影响动物成年后的移动效率。

paras.en: "This shows that animals -- and this probably includes humans -- can become more efficient based on their life experiences. So, when humans exercise regularly throughout our childhood and adolescence, it could build our capacity for exercise throughout our lives."
paras.zh: “这表明动物——可能包括人类——可以根据其生活经历变得更有效率。因此，当人类在整个童年和青春期定期锻炼时，可以增强我们一生的锻炼能力。”

paras.en: The findings provide new evidence that physical activity during development can have lasting effects on the energy required for movement. Whether the same adaptations occur in humans remains to be established, but the research suggests a potential mechanism through which childhood exercise could help support physical activity later in life.
paras.zh: 这些发现提供了新的证据，表明发育过程中的体力活动可以对运动所需的能量产生持久的影响。人类是否也会发生同样的适应仍有待确定，但研究表明，童年时期的锻炼可以帮助支持以后生活中的身体活动。

paras.en: Stephen Piazza, a professor of kinesiology at Penn State, also participated in the research, along with several current and former graduate students working with Piazza and Rubenson.
paras.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州立大学运动机能学教授斯蒂芬·皮亚扎（Stephen Piazza）以及与皮亚扎和鲁本森一起工作的几名现任和前任研究生也参与了这项研究。

paras.en: The study's two co-first authors were Talayah Johnson and Kavya Katugam-Dechene. Johnson completed her master's degree at Penn State and is now pursuing a doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania. Katugam-Dechene received her doctorate from Penn State and currently serves as a research assistant professor of biomedical and rehabilitation engineering at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.
paras.zh: 该研究的两位共同第一作者是 Talayah Johnson 和 Kavya Katugam-Dechene。约翰逊在宾夕法尼亚州立大学完成了硕士学位，目前正在宾夕法尼亚大学攻读博士学位。卡图甘-德切恩 (Katugam-Dechene) 在宾夕法尼亚州立大学获得博士学位，目前担任北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校生物医学和康复工程研究助理教授。

paras.en: Other contributors included Ian Dechene, who worked as research staff on the project and is now a software engineer, and Roberto Castro, a Penn State doctoral student jointly advised by Piazza and Rubenson.
paras.zh: 其他贡献者包括曾担任该项目研究人员、现为软件工程师的 Ian Dechene，以及由 Piazza 和 Rubenson 共同指导的宾夕法尼亚州立大学博士生 Roberto Castro。

paras.en: Funding was provided by the National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases, part of the National Institutes of Health, through awards R21AR071588 and R01AR080711. The researchers are solely responsible for the study's content, which does not necessarily reflect the official positions of the National Institutes of Health.
paras.zh: 美国国立卫生研究院下属的国家关节炎、肌肉骨骼和皮肤疾病研究所通过 R21AR071588 和 R01AR080711 奖项提供了资金。研究人员对研究内容全权负责，研究内容并不一定反映美国国立卫生研究院的官方立场。
